name: Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A)
latest_version: v1.0.1 (spec site labels 1.0.0 as latest released version)
governing_body: Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) under the Linux Foundation; hosted project since 2026-08-17 (previously Linux Foundation project since June 2025)
movement_implication: Standard interface for delegating a task to an independently hosted agent; it moves task requests and artifacts, not runtime checkpoints.
notes: v1.0.1 is a bug-fix release (HTTP binding media type, error transcoding, TaskStatus values). AAIF announcement: https://aaif.io/blog/a2a-joins-aaif

name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
governing_body: Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) under the Linux Foundation (founding project 2025-12-09)
movement_implication: Lets a delegated or relocated agent reach eligible tools through a uniform interface; 2026-07-28 removes protocol-level sessions and the initialize handshake, so per-connection server state no longer has to follow the client.
notes: Previous revision 2025-11-25. Tasks moved from core to an official extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks). Roots, Sampling and Logging deprecated. Versioning rules: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/versioning

name: Agent-User Interaction Protocol (AG-UI)
maturity: released 1.0 SDK; no formal stability statement found in docs
governing_body: Open-source community project originated by CopilotKit; no foundation or SDO stated
movement_implication: Carries the user-facing event stream and approvals, so a move can stay visible to the user; it does not transfer execution between runtimes.
notes: Monorepo publishes date-tagged releases; @ag-ui/a2a 0.0.7 bridges AG-UI 1.0 to A2A. Version and date from https://registry.npmjs.org/@ag-ui/core

name: Agent Communication Protocol (ACP; IBM / BeeAI)
governing_body: Linux Foundation (LF AI & Data); development wound down in favour of A2A
movement_implication: Do not target for new work; ACP users are directed to A2A, so A2A is the single delegation interface to track.
notes: Repository archived 2025-08-27 (GitHub banner). Not to be confused with the Agentic Commerce Protocol or Zed's Agent Client Protocol.

name: Agent Network Protocol (ANP)
maturity: stable per project for released parts; ANP-05/ANP-06 still draft
governing_body: ANP open-source community (no formal SDO stated in repository)
movement_implication: Decentralised alternative to A2A built on W3C DIDs (did:wba / did:web), relevant if agent identity must be portable without a central registry.
notes: Identity: ANP-02 (method-independent authentication) and ANP-03 (did:wba method).

name: AGNTCY Open Agentic Schema Framework (OASF)
maturity: stable (released schema versions are declared immutable)
governing_body: AGNTCY project under the Linux Foundation (since 2025-07-29)
movement_implication: Schema for describing agent capabilities and metadata, a candidate input for compatibility negotiation before a handoff.
notes: LF announcement: https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/linux-foundation-welcomes-the-agntcy-project-to-standardize-open-multi-agent-system-infrastructure-and-break-down-ai-agent-silos

name: Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
governing_body: Originated by Google; site states donation to FIDO Alliance with standardisation continuing in its Agentic Authentication technical work (donation date unverified)
movement_implication: Signed checkout/payment mandates show how user authority for a side-effecting action can travel with a delegated task as verifiable credentials.
notes: Positioned as an extension for A2A and MCP.

name: Agentic Commerce Protocol (OpenAI and Stripe)
governing_body: Maintained by OpenAI and Stripe (no SDO)
movement_implication: Example of a vendor-maintained interop spec for one side-effecting action class (checkout); relevant to idempotency and authority, not to general movement.
notes: Dated spec directories: 2025-09-29; 2025-12-12; 2026-01-16; 2026-01-30; 2026-04-17. No GitHub releases are published.

name: AGENTS.md
governing_body: Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) founding project (contributed by OpenAI)
movement_implication: Portable, repository-level instructions for coding agents; it moves guidance, not state or authority.
notes: Marginal to movement; tracked because it is an AAIF project.

name: Agent Skills
maturity: living format; allowed-tools field marked experimental
governing_body: Open community repository agentskills/agentskills (Apache-2.0); format originally developed by Anthropic and released as an open standard; not listed on aaif.io/projects
movement_implication: Portable procedure (instructions, references and executable scripts) that can be installed at a destination; it moves code but not state or authority, so treat it as software supply chain.
notes: scripts/ holds executable code that agents can run. Anthropic security guidance: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview (use only trusted sources). Trust gating for project-level skills: https://agentskills.io/client-implementation/adding-skills-support

name: WebMCP
maturity: draft (W3C Community Group report; not a W3C Standard nor on the W3C Standards Track)
governing_body: W3C Web Machine Learning Community Group
movement_implication: Web pages expose JavaScript tools to agents via document.modelContext.registerTool(); tools run in the page with the user's logged-in session, so authority stays with the browser and does not move with the agent.
notes: Origin trials in Chrome 149 and Edge 150 per https://github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp/blob/main/implementation-status.md (not checked against vendor pages).

name: WebDriver BiDi
governing_body: W3C Browser Testing and Tools Working Group
movement_implication: Standards-track bidirectional remote control of browsers; its storage module can read and set cookies, so a controller can copy a logged-in session, an authority-transfer path that needs policy.
notes: Modules: session, browser, browsingContext, emulation, network, script, storage, log, input, webExtension.

name: LangGraph persistence (langgraph-checkpoint + savers)
movement_implication: Checkpoints let a graph resume on another worker that runs compatible LangGraph code and the same saver backend; they are not a cross-framework format.
notes: Versions from https://pypi.org/pypi/langgraph-checkpoint/json and https://pypi.org/pypi/langgraph/json; postgres saver from the GitHub release checkpointpostgres==3.2.0. Docs page does not state cross-version checkpoint compatibility.

name: Temporal Server
movement_implication: Durable execution means a workflow can continue on any worker polling the same task queue, provided workflow code stays deterministic and activities are idempotent.
notes: Patch releases v1.31.4 and v1.30.8 also published 2026-10-12 for older lines.

name: Temporal SDKs (Go and Python)
movement_implication: Worker-side SDK version pinning matters for replay compatibility when a workflow resumes on a different worker.
notes: Other SDKs (Java/TypeScript/.NET) not checked.

name: OCI Image Format Specification
movement_implication: Makes the agent's code and runtime portable as an image; carries no live agent state.

name: OCI Runtime Specification
movement_implication: Defines how a container is run consistently across hosts; process checkpoint/restore (e.g. CRIU) is outside this spec.

name: OCI Distribution Specification
movement_implication: Registry API used to pull the same agent image at a destination; v1.1 referrers can attach signatures or SBOMs to that image.

name: Kubernetes
release_date: 1.37.0: 2026-08-26 (GitHub release); 1.37.1: 2026-09-15 per kubernetes.io/releases (GitHub release object published 2026-09-23)
movement_implication: Reschedules pods and Jobs after failure, which is restart, not migration; application-level checkpointing is still required.
notes: Supported minors listed: 1.37/1.36/1.35 (1.34 EOL 2026-10-27).

name: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693)
maturity: stable (IETF Proposed Standard; not updated or obsoleted per datatracker)
movement_implication: Standard way to exchange a token for a narrower, audience-bound token with actor (act) claims, the base pattern for delegated agent credentials.

name: Transaction Tokens (draft-ietf-oauth-transaction-tokens)
movement_implication: Short-lived tokens that carry user and request context through a chain of internal workloads, a candidate for propagating authority inside a multi-agent call chain.
notes: Internet-Draft; not an RFC.

name: OAuth Identity and Authorization Chaining Across Domains (draft-ietf-oauth-identity-chaining)
maturity: draft (IESG approved; in RFC Editor queue; intended Proposed Standard)
movement_implication: Combines token exchange with JWT grants to carry identity across trust domains, the closest IETF pattern for cross-organisation agent handoff.
notes: Not yet published as an RFC; RFC number unassigned as of access date.

name: WIMSE Architecture (draft-ietf-wimse-arch)
movement_implication: Architecture for workload identity across systems; agents are workloads, so this frames how a destination proves who it is.
notes: Related WG drafts: draft-ietf-wimse-workload-creds-02, draft-ietf-wimse-wpt-02, draft-ietf-wimse-http-signature-07.

name: AI Identity Management System (draft-ietf-wimse-aims)
movement_implication: First WG-adopted IETF draft specifically on AI-agent identity; content may change substantially.
notes: Replaces individual draft draft-klrc-aiagent-auth (-03).

name: OAuth 2.0 Extension: On-Behalf-Of User Authorization for AI Agents (draft-oauth-ai-agents-on-behalf-of-user)
movement_implication: Shows proposed on-behalf-of semantics for agents but carries no standards status; cite only as a proposal.

name: SPIFFE / SPIRE
latest_version: SPIRE v1.15.4 (SPIFFE spec: unversioned living spec)
movement_implication: Issues short-lived workload identities (SVIDs) to the process actually running, so identity is re-attested at the destination instead of copied.
notes: v1.14.8 patch also released 2026-10-15. CNCF page: https://www.cncf.io/projects/spire/

name: Open Policy Agent (OPA)
movement_implication: Policy-as-code engine that can gate whether a handoff, tool call or destination is allowed.
notes: CNCF page: https://www.cncf.io/projects/open-policy-agent-opa/

name: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (incl. agent spans and MCP)
latest_version: no tagged release in the new repository (main branch)
release_date: moved out of core semconv in v1.42.0 (2026-06-12)
movement_implication: Defines agent, model, tool and MCP span attributes for correlating a task across agents, but names may still change.
notes: opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/ now shows a 'moved' notice; gen_ai.* in the core repo is deprecated since v1.42.0.

name: OpenTelemetry semantic conventions (core)
maturity: mixed (per-convention stability; GenAI no longer included)
movement_implication: Core conventions (HTTP, RPC, Kubernetes) used to correlate the infrastructure side of a move.

name: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0
movement_implication: Format for signed, verifiable claims (e.g. delegated authority or attestation) that could travel with a task envelope.
notes: AP2 builds its mandates on verifiable digital credentials.

name: W3C Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) v1.0 / v1.1
movement_implication: Identifier scheme for agents that is not tied to one provider; used by ANP (did:wba / did:web).
notes: v1.0 Recommendation: https://www.w3.org/TR/did-core/
